bib.title: When a language model is optimized for reasoning, does it still show embers of autoregression? An analysis of OpenAI o1

question: Does o1, a model optimized for reasoning, still show the sensitivity to output probability and task frequency that earlier LLMs showed?
hypothesis: Optimizing for reasoning may reduce the limitations from next-word prediction, but o1's training likely also involved next-word prediction so the effects may persist.
contributions: Evaluates o1-preview on a subset of the Embers of Autoregression tasks
Shows o1 improves quantitatively but keeps output-probability sensitivity and some task-frequency sensitivity
Uses thinking-token counts as a second difficulty measure

method.summary: o1-preview-2024-09-12 was run with default settings on a subset of the tasks and datasets of McCoy et al. 2023, and compared with previously reported results for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude 3, Llama 3 and Gemini 1.0. Accuracy and median thinking tokens are compared across output-probability bins and common versus rare task variants, plus two harder variants to avoid ceiling effects.
method.task: Output-probability and task-frequency sensitivity on algorithmic string tasks

datasets.name: Embers of Autoregression task datasets (subset)
datasets.source: McCoy et al. 2023; large datasets excluded because of o1 cost per example
datasets.preprocessing: Harder sorting: all words start with the letter i. Shift cipher: examples binned by output log probability.

other.note: results taken from McCoy et al. 2023

inference.prompting: not stated; refers to McCoy et al. 2023

parameters.tasks_output_probability: shift cipher decoding, Pig Latin decoding, article swapping, word-list reversal
parameters.tasks_task_frequency: shift cipher decoding (13 vs 12), Pig Latin encoding, acronyms (first vs second letter), linear function, sorting (alphabetical vs reverse)

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of examples answered correctly; error bars one standard error

metrics.name: Thinking tokens
metrics.definition: median number of tokens in o1's chain of thought per group of examples

eval.protocol: One standard error intervals; no significance tests stated; number of examples and runs not stated.

evidence.quote: The version of o1 used for all results below is o1-preview-2024-09-12, which we tested with its default settings.

results.claim: o1 shift cipher accuracy rises with output probability, from lowest to highest bin.
results.setup: o1-preview, shift cipher decoding, lowest vs highest output-probability bin
results.quote: its accuracy ranges from 47% in the lowest-probability case to 92% in the highest-probability case

results.claim: On acronyms o1 scored near-identically on common and rare variants, yet used far more tokens on the rare one.
results.quote: for acronyms, o1 achieved 100% accuracy on the common variant and 99.9% accuracy on the rare variant

results.claim: o1 uses more thinking tokens on low-probability outputs across all four tasks.
results.note: Magnitudes only in the figure (axis to 6000)

results.claim: On the standard datasets o1 is far better than other LLMs on rare variants and shows similar scores on common and rare; this may be a ceiling effect.
With harder sorting (all words start with i) and medium/low-probability shift cipher examples, o1 does better on the common variant than the rare one.

limits: Only a subset of tasks, excluding large datasets because of o1 cost per example
o1 internals are not public; the explanations for probability sensitivity are speculation
Chain-of-thought contents are hidden; only token counts are visible
Ceiling effects on standard datasets limit conclusions about task frequency
Only o1-preview tested; other models' results are copied from 2023
No example counts, runs, prompts or significance tests are given; most numbers are in figures only

terms.definition: behavioral patterns that result from the influence of being optimized to perform next-word prediction
analyze the system through the lens of the pressures that have shaped it
